_about: PLAINTEXT ANSWERS — the source of truth for content/hackillinois-2027/challenges.json. This file is NOT served and NOT copied into the Docker image; only the generated digests travel with the pack. Edit here, then run `npm run gauntlet:hashes -- hackillinois-2027`. Never hand-edit the generated file.

challenges.title: Off by one

cases.input: The result of running the snippet

challenges.title: Two seats, fifty people
Snap to the grid
challenges.prompt:
Positions are published snapped to a 20-metre grid, using:

  Math.round(x / 20) * 20

A trainer stands at x = 51. What x is published?

challenges.title: The three-way ring
challenges.prompt:
Alice wants Bob's shift, Bob wants Charlie's, and Charlie wants Alice's. The resolver enumerates elementary cycles of length 2 to 4 by depth-first search, refusing to traverse below the start node.

How many distinct cycles does it find in this graph?

challenges.title: The guard that cannot fire
choices: The sample is kept, because accuracy is unknown
The sample is dropped, every time

cases.input: The outcome for a device with no accuracy figure

challenges.title: The loser of a compare-and-set
challenges.prompt:
Two requests read the same document at version 7 and both try:

  findOneAndUpdate({ _id, version: 7 }, { $inc: { version: 1 } })

How many of the two get a document back?

challenges.title: Fuzzed to a grid
challenges.prompt:
Published positions are snapped to a 20 m grid with Math.round(x / 20) * 20, then nudged by a stable per-hour offset of up to 8 m.

A trainer at x = 31 is published. What is the largest x a viewer could see?

challenges.title: The seat that never opens
challenges.prompt:
A shift has 2 seats and 48 people waitlisted. One confirmed volunteer cancels, and the server promotes the head of the waitlist inside the same request, holding the seat across the whole cascade.

How many seats are claimable by a new arrival during that request?

challenges.title: Scanned twice
challenges.prompt:
An attendance token is HMAC'd, rotates every 30 seconds, and is single-use via a unique index on its nonce.

Two desks scan the same photographed token at the same instant, inside the window. What happens?
choices: One checks in, one gets a 409

challenges.title: The cap that was not there

cases.input: Daily ceiling for an unpriced source

challenges.title: Rings in a wants-graph
challenges.prompt:
Four volunteers want each other's shifts: A wants B's, B wants A's, C wants D's, D wants C's.

The resolver enumerates elementary cycles of length 2 to 4, refusing to traverse below the start node. How many does it find?

challenges.title: Sliced, not pinned
challenges.prompt:
The presence tick yields to the event loop every 8 ms, but only checks the clock every 32nd session rather than every one.

Can a single contiguous block exceed 8 ms?
choices: No — 8 ms is a hard ceiling
Yes — slicing bounds the block, it does not pin it under the budget
Only when there are fewer than 32 sessions

cases.input: Whether a block can exceed the budget
